newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OILERS DUMP KINGS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OILERS DUMP KINGS.

text.p: EDMONTON, March 5 (Reuter0 - Mariusz Czerkawski scored twice and set up another goal as the Edmonton Oilers defeated the Los Angeles Kings, 4-1, ending their season-high five-game winning streak on Tuesday.
Jason Arnott added a goal and three assists and Curtis Joseph made 28 saves for Edmonton.

Czerkawski, who has 10 points in his last seven games, scored a power-play goal with 3:55 left in the first period, giving the Oilers a 2-0 lead. He tallied again at 8:37 of the third to restore Edmonton's two-goal cushion and set up Arnott's goal 27 seconds later to seal the Oilers' second win in 10 games (2-6-2).
Vitali Yachmenev had the lone goal for Los Angeles.
At the Islanders, Dino Ciccarelli had two goals and an assist and Chris Gratton also scored twice, leading the surging Tampa Bay Lightning to a 6-3 victory over the New York Islanders.

Red-hot Rick Tabaracci made 28 saves, including 11 in the third period, for the Lightning, who improved to 7-1-1 in their last nine games and extended their unbeaten streak against New York to six games (5-0-1).
"Overall, Tabaracci saved our rear end in the last five minutes," Tampa Bay coach Terry Crisp said. "This Islander team has some serious speed, they came in waves tonight."

In Pittsburgh, Doug Gilmour had a goal and an assist and Mike Dunham and Martin Brodeur combined for 21 saves as the red-hot New Jersey Devils defeated the Pittsburgh Penguins, 3-1, spoiling Craig Patrick's return to coaching.

Gilmour has a point in each of his four games with New Jersey, totalling four goals and five assists since he was acquired February 25th in a six-player trade from Toronto. In 20 games since the All-Star break, he has nine goals and 23 assists.
"I think the biggest thing when you (get) a team like this, you just try to get in the flow, stay out of the way and that's what I'm trying to do at this point," Gilmour said.
Bill Guerin and John MacLean had the other goals for the Devils.

In Washington, Newly acquired Bill Ranford stopped 29 shots and Adam Oates scored his first goal since being acquired in the same trade last week as the Washington Capitals edged the Calgary Flames, 2-1.
Ranford, who was picked up with Oates and winger Rick Tocchet from Boston, made just six saves in the final period but came up big in the first.

"It was a little nerve-racking tonight because I didn't know what to expect," Ranford said. "But this team plays such good defence. I was excited tonight. Oates played great tonight. I don't think either of us slept well this afternoon because we were a little nervous."
